segments.title: 2. Text -> character -> sprite sheet + FBX
lines: No photo? Describe a FICTIONAL character in a text spec (key = value lines).
The studio builds a 3D mannequin from it (procedural, no AI), poses every move,
renders the sprite sheet and exports a rigged model.glb + model.fbx.
It is a stylised mannequin, not a likeness - never use it to imitate a real person.

script.cap: 'New spec from template...' / 'Edit spec...' opens the built-in editor with every key explained
Save & use - the spec file is now the input
Step 2 - output: pick a profile, e.g. platformer (Godot SpriteFrames, Unity JSON, Tiled tileset)
GLB model + FBX ticked: a rigged 3D model with one take per move (FBX needs Blender installed)
Posing the mannequin for each move, rendering frames, writing the sheet + manifests + GLB + FBX
Done: pick any move in the preview to play it (here: run)
The log lists the profile files: nova_runner.tres (Godot), .unity.json, .tsx (Tiled), model.glb, model.fbx

items: preview.png: every move of the sheet (atlas.png)
model.fbx re-imported in Blender: mesh + armature + one take per move. Import it in Unity / Unreal / Godot / Blender

segments.title: Limits (honest)
lines: The mannequin is low-poly and stylised; face detail is minimal.
Spec keys like ethnicity are metadata only - skin_tone sets the colour.
FBX is converted from the GLB by Blender (needs Blender 3.6+ / 4.x installed).
Next: video 3 - using the sheet in a game, and console exports.
